- Given accomplishments (numbered claims)
Required:
A) Three real risks in ToUnicode fix (when corrupts correct text? cases should not apply?) and how detect automatically.
B) What remains unproven.
C) Plan next cycle: 5 steps ordered by impact/cost, with exit gate for each.
D) One design flaw not mentioned — if I see it.
Tag every claim: مثبت/مرجح/مجهول. Arabic, no intro.

Need think carefully. Need produce concise but thorough. Need hostile review. Need label each assertion. Could use bullet points. Need ensure tags: every claim? Likely tag items [مثبت], [مرجح], [مجهول]. We need base on provided info but adversarial. Need analyze PDF fonts, ToUnicode, Type0, Type3, Chrome printing, U+200F RLM, space mapping. Arabic text? Need Arabic. No intro.

Important technical details:
- Chrome maps space to U+200F (RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK) instead of U+0020 in ToUnicode? It says إصلاح post-process rewrites glyph mapping in ToUnicode (no text, no position). Effect: line-order metric 0.360 -> 0.920.
Risks:
1) If glyph legitimately maps to U+200F (RLM) or control/format chars, replacing all U+200F to U+0020 will corrupt actual intended RLM, ZWJ/ZWNJ? Could break bidi, ligatures, or invisible chars. Detection: only rewrite CID/glyph whose width/advance equals space? Need validate via cmap, original font CMap, GSUB? If font's space glyph name is space/uni0020 and original Unicode is U+200F? Hmm.
2) If ToUnicode maps ligature or glyph to U+200F due to Chrome bug? But U+200F might be used as fallback for missing glyphs or marks? Rewriting can collapse distinct invisible characters, harm copy/search/accessibility, semantic. Need detect: check glyph coverage and original text? compare extraction before/after; use actual rendered positions? Use font encoding/ToUnicode only if glyph index corresponds to space in font; require glyph name or cmap. If font has multiple glyphs mapping to U+200F, don't rewrite. If the font is symbolic/non-Unicode, risky.
3) If PDF has existing correct ToUnicode for some fonts or subsets where U+200F intentionally maps to spacing glyph for justification/kashida? Changing could alter logical text order, bidi, line breaks. Also if document uses U+200F for bidi control in Arabic, replacing with space introduces visible spaces, disrupts script shaping if re-extracted text re-rendered. Detect by checking document's original source text? If no source, use heuristic: only apply when extracted sequence U+200F occurs between Arabic letters with no advance? Actually space has width, RLM zero-width. If glyph advance width > 0? U+200F is zero width. If glyph has positive width and name space, likely bug. But if PDF uses visible blank? Need check. If advance zero, don't map to space. Also check OS/2 metrics? If width matches font's space width. Use PDF font resources /BaseFont /FontDescriptor, embedded font cmap. Verify glyph name. Need automated: parse CIDToGIDMap, ToUnicode CMap, font cmap, glyph advance widths, glyph names. Only rewrite mapping for glyph IDs that (a) advance equals space, (b) original font cmap maps U+0020 to same GID or glyph name is space, (c) no other codepoint maps to that GID, (d) context not part of actual RLM? But if Chrome generated ToUnicode has U+200F for space, original embedded font might be subset missing U+0020? Need check.
Also risk: patching ToUnicode only fixes extraction, not actual content stream. If consumers use actual text (marked content, ActualText) or rendering? It might create mismatch between visual and logical text. If PDF/UA or accessibility requires correct ActualText? Could break PDF/A? veraPDF may still pass if ToUnicode valid? But PDF/A requires ToUnicode for all fonts? Changing may affect conformance if mapping to not present? Need mention.
Another risk: If multiple fonts share same ToUnicode? rewriting globally could affect other glyphs. Or patching wrong stream because compression, object streams. Need detect via checksums, round-trip, validate.

B) Unproven:
- That fix doesn't corrupt other documents/fonts/Chrome versions, cross-platform. Only one metric improved; no ground truth text extraction, search, copy/paste, screen readers, accessibility, PDF/UA, long-term preservation. Need proven.
- That five fixed weights truly solve all variable font issue; Type3 may still appear under other axes, fallback, UI, dynamic text, non-Latin? Need prove.
- That font_intake guarantees no shaping/joining issues? It checks GSUB/GPOS presence but not correctness, feature coverage, required ligatures, mark positioning quality, Unicode coverage, variable font behavior, subsetting, embedding licenses.
- That Chrome prints what? The portal reads Chrome-printed PDF, but not proof for other renderers, OS print stacks, PDF viewers, Acrobat, Ghostscript, MuPDF variants. Need prove.
- That line-order metric 0.920 is sufficient/meaningful; not proven user-visible correctness. Need human evaluation.
- That dropping diacritics claim is acceptable; not proven for all faces, all marks, all renderers.
- That PDF/A-3b with embedded file? veraPDF zero errors doesn't guarantee archival suitability, font licensing, metadata, XMP, associated files.
- That U+200F bug only space; maybe other characters mapped wrong. Need full char mapping audit.
- That no form fields? maybe not proven with all tools.

C) Plan next cycle: 5 steps ordered by impact/cost, each exit gate. Need likely high impact low cost first. Maybe:
1) Freeze ground-truth regression corpus + automatic oracle for extraction (screen and print), with exact expected Unicode, order, and prohibited mappings. Exit: 100% of corpus has expected files, metrics baseline, CI runs, all current artifacts reproduce.
2) Make ToUnicode fix conservative and testable: whitelist glyph-by-glyph rewrite based on embedded font cmap/glyph name/advance; add dry-run, report all candidate mappings, refuse if ambiguous. Exit: zero rewrites on negative controls, correct rewrite on known Chrome space bug, all PDF/A and text extraction tests pass, no change to non-space chars.
3) Replace/avoid runtime patch by fixing source or printing pipeline: ensure actual U+0020 in text or use ActualText/marked content? Maybe if possible use source HTML/CSS and font settings, or generate PDF via a controlled engine. Exit: new PDF from pipeline passes extraction without post-process for 100% of test pages; if impossible, document fallback.
4) Expand font intake from presence checks to behavioral conformance: for each accepted font, automated shaping samples, space mapping, subset/embedding test, print from Chrome to PDF, extract text, check no Type3, features. Exit: 5 weights + any future font pass all behavioral tests; failing fonts rejected with reasons.
5) Build viewer/consumer acceptance matrix + accessibility/validation: MuPDF, pdfium, Acrobat? Ghostscript, screen reader? PDF/UA? Search/copy. Exit: N viewers pass extraction/search/order, veraPDF PDF/A, no regressions, signed report. Or risk monitoring.
Need order by impact/cost. Could be: (1) ground truth; (2) conservative patch; (3) root cause mitigation; (4) behavioral font intake; (5) external validation. Include exit gates.

D) One design flaw not mentioned. Need identify. They mention two versions screen/print, strip nav from markup, portal reads Chrome printed PDF. ToUnicode fix post-process. Possible design flaw: relying on Chrome's print pipeline as source of truth and patching symptoms after generation, instead of controlling PDF generation or using tagged/accessible PDF with marked content/ActualText. Or: having screen/print two divergent sources creates dual maintenance and semantic drift; strip nav from markup before print can cause mismatch between screen DOM and PDF content, making links/pages and accessibility inconsistent. Or: using ToUnicode patch without altering content stream creates a lie: extracted text differs from actual encoded text / rendering, dangerous for accessibility, search, PDF/UA, legal archival. Which one is "one design flaw not mentioned"? Need choose one. They ask "عيب واحد في التصميم لم أذكره — إن رأيته." We can say: treating post-process ToUnicode as a product-level fix while the PDF content stream remains wrong; you are patching metadata not text, creating divergence and hiding upstream bug. Or maybe design flaw: the portal reads only Chrome's output, but the standard should be renderer-agnostic; if all decisions based on Chrome, you're coupling to a bug. Need pick one. They already mention Chrome bug and post-process. They maybe didn't mention that patch only ToUnicode means extracted text is corrected but not the PDF's actual text object, so copy/search works but accessibility/ActualText, tagged PDF, text reflow, and any consumer that uses content stream (or glyph indices) still broken. But they said "لا نص، لا موضع" and aware. Could be design flaw: using U+200F as space means directionality/control char in extraction; ToUnicode fix hides that but if PDF is later edited, merged, linearized, or reprocessed by tools that rebuild ToUnicode, fix may be lost. Another: two versions (screen/print) and portal reading Chrome output creates untrusted chain; the printable version is a derived artifact with no single source of truth. Need pick robust.
